name: Cathédrale Notre-Dame-de-l'Assomption de Clermont-Ferrand
elevationDatum: Rigid local exterior foundation plane y=0; metres +X east, +Y up, +Z south. Mapped rotation baked once. No sea-level, DEM or Mercator scaling.
note: Dark volcanic-stone Gothic cathedral with unequal twin western needle spires, true pierced bell stages and pointed windows, an eight-and-a-half-metre rose, sixteen open flying buttresses, polygonal choir and the smaller Bayette bell tower. Published 99 m length and 32.7 m transept width are not identical to the OSM outer building polygon, which includes chapels and buttress projections and is approximately 90 × 44 m in the local frame. The mapped body is retained and the western access stair extends the full model close to 99 m; that interpretation is an estimate, not a surveyed reconciliation. Roof ridge 40 m, western tower subdivisions and Bayette placement within the mapped north transept are photo-derived estimates. The official site rounds both spires to 96.10 m; the documented 95.50 m southern tip is retained. No statues, stained-glass artwork, text, neighbouring buildings or terrain are reproduced. Rigid y=0 is the exterior foundation/contact plane, not altitude. Cityscape: not tested. Full 3D world: not tested.
